question: Which of the following is true for resistors in parallel?

options.text: The equivalent resistance is greater than the smallest resistance.
The equivalent resistance is the sum of all resistances.

solution:
The correct answer is __They have the same voltage**(Option 4)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resistors in parallel__ have the same voltage across them.
 
• The equivalent resistance in a parallel circuit is always less than the smallest individual resistance.
 
• Resistors in parallel share the total current, which is distributed among them based on their resistance values.
 
• The formula to calculate the equivalent resistance in parallel is 1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ...
 
• This configuration is often used in electrical systems to provide multiple paths for current flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistors in Series:**
 
 
• In a series circuit, the current is the same through all resistors, but the voltage is divided among them.
 
• The equivalent resistance in series is the sum of all resistances.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuit Applications:**
 
 
• Used in household electrical systems to ensure devices operate independently.
 
• Improves reliability, as one component failure does not affect others.
 
 
 
• **Energy Considerations:**
 
 
• Parallel circuits consume more power since the total resistance decreases.
 
• Efficient for applications requiring consistent voltage.
